item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-04 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IINF-01 Elettronica

AI workloads on space and defence platforms, such as on-board satellite image processing, autonomous navigation and multi-sensor fusion, must run under tight power, reliability and certification constraints, which favour compact, programmable vector processors over fixed-function accelerators. Their efficiency depends largely on the compiler. This Incarico di Ricerca, aligned with the activity of the ARCHYTAS project, focuses on the LLVM compiler infrastructure for vector processors based on the RISC-V Vector (RVV) extension. The research program involves the design, construction, and testing of electronic devices capable of detecting vibrations and sounds generated within the human body. The project stems from the need to bridge the gap between the evolution of the vehicle fleet, characterized by increasing vehicle masses and dimensions, and the current UNECE, Euro NCAP and EN 1317 regulatory frameworks.
